title: HERV proteogenomics of narcotic-driven HIV latency
text:
We know very little about the relationship between HIV and endogenous retroviruses in the brain. We propose
to use a combination of newly developed technologies to investigate the implications of narcotics on
endogenous retroviruses expression in the context of HIV latency in primary human microglia cells.

title: Targeting Nr2e3 to prevent photoreceptor degeneration
text:
Mutations in dozens of different genes cause photoreceptor degeneration and blindness, but there is currently
no effective therapy for these disorders. In this proposal we will develop a novel strategy to prevent blindness
which utilizes CRISPR-Cas9 technology to knock out a key photoreceptor transcription factor, thereby
suppressing photoreceptor degeneration. We believe that this new therapy will be applicable to multiple
genetically distinct forms of blindness.

title: Tumor-activatable Interleukin-2 Superkine Nanoparticle Therapy
text:
This R01 application will focus on the development of tumor-activatable IL-2 superkine nanoparticles for
cancer immunotherapy. Delivery of Rb-tropic, acidity-resistant IL-2 superkine by UPS nanoparticles will
effectively mask the systemic toxicity in normal tissues while achieving robust activation of cytotoxic
lymphocytes in tumors for efficacious therapy.

title: SCH: Multi-modal Biosensing and Predictive Analytics for Continuous Monitoring of Mobility and Cognition in an Aging Population
text:
RELEVANCE (See instructions):
The proposed project will develop and test an easy-to-use multi-modal monitoring system of sensors and
data processing algorithms intended for use by older adults to reveal subtle changes in cognition and
mobility, both early indicators of pending Alzheimer's disease and related dementia. This will provide
important insight into an early window for interventions to delay or prevent the onset of these devastating

title: Modifiable Mechanisms Linking Chronic Pain to Suicide Risk
text:
Suicide risk is significantly elevated among individuals with chronic pain, yet the mechanisms linking pain and
suicide remain poorly understood. Emerging evidence suggests that cognitive-affective vulnerabilities, such as
intolerance of uncertainty and anxiety sensitivity, may intensify pain-related distress and increase motivation for
relief through suicidal thoughts and behavior. This study aims to test this model using laboratory and real-world
methods, laying the groundwork for targeted, personalized suicide prevention strategies in individuals living with
chronic pain.

title: Next-generation alchemical free energy methods and quantum/machine-learning models for drug discovery
text:
Next-generation alchemical free energy methods and quantum/machine-learning
 models for drug discovery.
PI: Darrin M. York, Rutgers University, Piscataway, NJ 08854-8087 USA.
 The current proposal addresses a critical barrier to progress in drug discovery: limitations
in precision and accuracy of alchemical free energy simulations for prediction of ligand-protein
binding afﬁnities. Speciﬁcally, new advanced technologies are proposed to enhance precision in
alchemical free energy simulations, and a new quantum mechanical/deep-learning potential force
ﬁeld is developed to improve accuracy of binding afﬁnity predictions. Methods and models will
be carefully validated against several targets in collaboration with both academic and industry
researchers.

title: Dynamics and molecular mechanisms linking metabolism and the epigenome
text:
To effectively perform their function, each cell type in the human body must respond
appropriately to incoming signals and cells enlist specific machines to carryout cell-type unique
instructions, a layer of information (called the epigenome) on top of the genome. This proposal
will investigate how these molecular machines ‘interpret’ incoming signals, ‘read’ the existing
epigenetic landscape and ‘respond’ appropriately. Knowledge of this communication network is
key to understanding how major breakdowns in information flow, either as a lack of response to
extra-cellular signals or to an ill-advised decision, leads to disease states.

title: Mechanistic role of GPR6 in therapy resistance and its antibody-based targeting in prostate cancer
text:
Public Relevance (Narrative)
This project addresses treatment-induced neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC), an
aggressive and therapy-resistant subtype of prostate cancer with no effective treatments. We will
investigate the role of the G protein–coupled receptor GPR6, which is elevated in NEPC and
drives tumor progression and therapy resistance, using state-of-the-art preclinical models. Newly
developed monoclonal antibodies that specifically block GPR6 will be tested as powerful research
tools and as potential therapeutic candidates for advanced prostate cancer.

title: Protein kinase C signaling in prostate cancer health disparities
text:
The main goal in this application is to establish whether the kinase PKCa contributes to phenotypic and
outcome disparities observed in PCa in AA men. Our studies identified the kinase PKCa as an essential player
in prostate cancer cell growth, tumorigenesis and invasion. We speculate that cancer cell PKCa plays a major
role in the regulation of cytokine production and tumor immune cell populations, which contributes to PCa racial
disparities.

title: Roles of Glycosylation and Deglycosylation During Animal Development
text:
Addition of carbohydrates to animal proteins (glycosylation) regulates many aspects of embryonic development
and adult physiology, and results in a host of human diseases when impaired. The proposed studies aim to
identify target proteins that mediate the effects of glycosylation and deglycosylation in developing animals and
might provide a better understanding of the pathophysiology of glycosylation disorders.

title: Machine-Learning Prediction and Reducing Overdoses with EHR Nudges (mPROVEN)
text:
The US continues to grapple with an opioid epidemic, with close to 70,000 opioid overdose deaths in 2020.
This project will test whether combining machine-learning based overdose risk prediction tools with simple
behavioral ‘nudge’ interventions in the electronic health record can improve clinician prescribing behavior to
reduce overdose risk. If successful, the project will demonstrate how risk prediction can help target low cost
and scalable interventions to reduce overdose risk, opening the door to larger scale implementation and
substantial public health benefit.

title: Evaluation of clinical and social factors associated with deficit accumulation trajectories in older survivors with early-stage non-small cell lung cancer
text:
Aging involves a gradual clinical decline in cognitive and physical function and often the development of
various comorbidities. However, significant life events, such as a cancer diagnosis, cancer treatment, or other
individual-level and societal-level factors can accelerate clinical decline and aging in cancer survivors
compared to other older people without a cancer diagnosis. The completion of this study will identify targetable
multilevel aging risk factors in the older population with lung cancer, as well as provide a valuable monitoring
tool to predict dynamic risk of aging-related clinical decline, allowing for a deeper understanding of drivers of
aging acceleration and timely intervention before clinical decline occurs.

title: The biochemical mechanism and pharmacological inhibition of phosphatidylinositol phosphate kinases
text:
The phosphatidylinositol phosphate kinases are responsible for the synthesis of two functionally
important phosphatidylinositol bisphosphates, PI(4,5)P2 and PI(3,5)P2. Biochemical and
crystallographic experiments are planned in this application to study how this family of lipid kinases
achieves substrate specificity and how pharmacological inhibition of one family member, PIKfyve,
could disrupt SARS-CoV-2 replication in cell culture models.

title: Lineage tracing origins of human innate lymphoid cells from hematopoietic precursors
text:
Natural killer cells are immune cells that play a critical role in controlling viral infections and fighting cancer.
Despite their importance, little is known about how developing NK cells receive signals required for their
differentiation. This project will generate novel lineage tracing methods to define emergence of human NK cells
from multipotent progenitors and define the transcriptomic trajectories of human NK cells.

title: A comprehensive study of tandem repeat variation as a cause of Alzheimer's disease
text:
Although >40 tandem repeat expansions (TREs) have been identified in a variety of late-onset neurological
diseases, including in patients diagnosed with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and dementia, there have been no
concerted efforts to systematically screen for novel TREs in AD cohorts. Similarly, recent studies have
identified copy number variations in large tandem repeats as a risk factor for Alzheimer’s disease. Using novel
bioinformatics approaches, in this proposal we will analyze exome sequencing data from ~62,000 AD samples
and controls generated by the Alzheimer's Disease Sequencing Project, supplemented with ~48,000 TOPMed
controls, to identify novel TREs and tandem repeat variants that are responsible for AD.

title: Corneal and Schwann cell mechanisms in vesicant injury
text:
We will combine the use of transgenic and gene knockout systems with proteomic and transcriptomic
approaches to study chemical injury in the cornea and interrogate these findings to illuminate new
biomarkers and effectors of corneal injury and unravel repair mechanisms that have not been previously
established.

title: A Remote Intervention to Prevent Overdose among People who Use Stimulants and/or Opioids
text:
This Type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation randomized controlled trial, A Remote Intervention to Prevent
Overdose among People who Use Stimulants and/or Opioids, aims to address the United States overdose
crisis driven by fentanyl and other synthetic opioids by reducing overdose rates. This study will be the first
national, fully remote trial to isolate the independent impact of overdose prevention education on overdose
outcomes. Findings will directly inform scalable, low-barrier models capable of reaching rural and underserved
populations not currently engaged in substance use services.

title: Integrating neural and momentary assessment of parenting, arousal, and adolescent substance use
text:
My NIH-funded program of research uses laboratory and fMRI methods to examine sex differences in
parenting effects on mechanisms of the development of substance use in adolescence. This proposed
Independent Scientist K02 Award would provide me with crucial advanced training to enhance my career and
transform my program of research by integrating ecological momentary assessment (EMA) science to
understand from a neural and momentary level parenting, emotion, and substance use associations. It would
also support a research study that would add EMA data collection to my already-recruited longitudinal cohort of
adolescents to examine the interplay between neural responses (in fMRI) and momentary vulnerabilities to
support future developmental studies and smart-phone delivered momentary intervention development studies.

title: Transcatheter Intra-Arterial Delivery of Oriented Anti-PD-L1 Immune checkpoint inhibitors Immobilized Nanocarriers for Local Combination Immunotherapy of Hepatocellular Carcinoma
text:
We propose image guided transcatheter intra-arterial (IA) delivery of Z-domain mediated aPD-L1 conjugated
ferumoxytol (aPD-L1-Z-Fer) permitting combinational local immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) immunotherapy
and irreversible electroporation (IRE) of hepatocellular carcinoma. Selective transcatheter IA delivery of our
aPD-L1-Z-Fer in a combination with immunogenic IRE treatment will permit efficient local delivery of
immunostimulatory ICB molecules, allow an increase in the dosage and improve their safety profile. This salient
combination of local ICB immunotherapy and immunogenic IRE offers the potential to significantly improve
longitudinal treatment outcomes in liver cancer.

title: Developing Gene Editing Therapeutics, Biodegradable Polymeric Delivery Vehicles, and High-throughput Platforms for the Treatment of Cystic Fibrosis
text:
The proposed research is directly relevant to public health in that it is aimed at developing a cure for
cystic fibrosis and incorporates key steps towards the clinical translation of a therapeutic. Further, the research
will develop tools for therapeutic screening and enhancing fundamental knowledge of drug delivery mechanisms.
Overall, this work has the potential to contribute to the treatment of devastating genetic diseases, significantly
improving the health of patients and reducing the burden of illness.
